Goblet cells.prompt: Mucus-secreting goblet cells from human intestinal epithelium. These specialized secretory cells produce and release gel-forming mucins that form the protective mucus layer of the gastrointestinal tract, expressing MUC2, TFF3, and FCGBP.

Purkinje cells.prompt: Purkinje neurons from human cerebellar cortex. Large GABAergic inhibitory neurons in the Purkinje layer of the cerebellum, characterized by extensive dendritic arbors and expression of CALB1, PCP2, and ITPR1.

Podocytes.prompt: Glomerular podocytes from human kidney. Highly specialized epithelial cells wrapping the capillaries of the renal glomerulus, forming the slit diaphragm filtration barrier and expressing NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1, and PODXL.

Leydig cells.prompt: Interstitial Leydig cells from human testis. Steroidogenic cells located in the interstitial compartment between seminiferous tubules, responsible for testosterone biosynthesis and expressing STAR, CYP11A1, and HSD3B2.

Club cells.prompt: Non-ciliated bronchiolar club cells (formerly Clara cells) from human distal airways. Secretory epithelial cells expressing SCGB1A1 and CYP2F1, contributing to airway surface liquid and xenobiotic metabolism in the terminal bronchioles.

Merkel cells.prompt: Merkel cells from human skin epidermis. Neuroendocrine mechanoreceptor cells in the basal layer of the epidermis, associated with light-touch sensation and expressing KRT20, ATOH1, and ISL1.

informal_cd8.free_form_prompt: immune cells that kill infected cells in the lung
informal_cd8.structured_prompt: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes from human lung tissue. Adaptive immune cells expressing CD8A, CD8B, GZMB, PRF1, and IFNG.

informal_macrophage.free_form_prompt: the big cells that eat bacteria and dead cells in inflamed tissue
informal_macrophage.structured_prompt: Macrophages from human inflamed tissue. Innate immune phagocytic cells expressing CD68, CD163, CSF1R, and MRC1.

informal_stem.free_form_prompt: undifferentiated cells that can become many different cell types in the bone marrow
informal_stem.structured_prompt: Hematopoietic stem cells from human bone marrow. Multipotent progenitor cells expressing CD34, KIT, THY1, and CXCR4.

informal_neuron.free_form_prompt: brain cells that fire electrical signals and talk to each other with chemicals
informal_neuron.structured_prompt: Excitatory neurons from human cerebral cortex. Glutamatergic neurons expressing SLC17A7, RBFOX3, SNAP25, and SYN1.

verbose_treg.free_form_prompt: I am looking for a type of T cell that suppresses immune responses rather than promoting them. They are often found in tumors and express FOXP3 and CD25. Sometimes called regulatory T cells.
verbose_treg.structured_prompt: CD4+ regulatory T cells from human tumor microenvironment. Immunosuppressive T lymphocytes expressing FOXP3, IL2RA, CTLA4, and IKZF2.

question_style.free_form_prompt: what would a fibroblast in a wound healing context look like at the single-cell level
question_style.structured_prompt: Activated fibroblasts from human wound healing tissue. Mesenchymal cells expressing COL1A1, ACTA2, FAP, and POSTN.

shorthand_nk.structured_prompt: Natural killer cells from human peripheral blood. Cytotoxic innate lymphocytes expressing NCAM1, KLRD1, NKG7, and GNLY.

clinical_note_style.free_form_prompt: Patient sample shows atypical large B-cells consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, germinal center subtype
clinical_note_style.structured_prompt: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cells, germinal center subtype, from human lymph node. Malignant B lymphocytes expressing BCL6, CD10, LMO2, and CD20.

summary.interpretation: Marker hit rate measures whether genes named in the prompt appear in the top 25% of expressed genes in the generated cells. A high rate suggests text-conditional generation; a low rate suggests the model ignores specific gene references and falls back to generic expression profiles. Expression cosine similarity between free-form and structured equivalents measures whether informal prompts produce similar profiles to template-style prompts.
summary.decoder_collapse_note: All free-form vs. structured expression cosines are 1.0 because the scGPT decoder produces identical expression profiles regardless of the input embedding. The text conditioning generates distinct latent representations (cosine sim 0.39-0.54 in DiT output space), but these differences are lost in scGPT decoding.

embedding_differentiation.description: While conditioning vectors and DiT latent embeddings differentiate between prompts, the scGPT decoder collapses all latent variation to near-identical expression profiles.

test_prompts.free_cd8: immune cells that kill infected cells in the lung
test_prompts.struct_cd8: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes from human lung tissue expressing CD8A CD8B GZMB PRF1 IFNG
test_prompts.free_neuron: brain cells that fire electrical signals and talk to each other with chemicals

embedding_differentiation.conclusion: The text conditioning pipeline (CLOP + DiT) produces differentiated latent representations, but the frozen scGPT decoder maps all embeddings to near-identical expression profiles. This confirms the decoder-dominance artifact: reported gene-level correlations reflect decoder reconstruction rather than generation fidelity.
